problem: Image-relative topological maps lack geometric understanding, and object-relative maps (ObjectReact's WayObject costmap) give coarse costs that discard fine geometric gradients. Metric maps need globally consistent geometry.
motivation: A controller needs a dense, informative planning signal and should be robust to planning errors. MASt3R gives dense correspondences and relative 3D point maps, which allows a geometrically precise map without global consistency.
key_idea: Build a pixel-level topological graph from MASt3R correspondences (zero-cost inter-image edges, 3D-distance intra-image edges), run Dijkstra to get a dense WayPixel costmap, and condition a learned controller (PixelReact) on it.
insight: Pixel-level costs are a better conditioning variable than object-level ones: the ObjectReact controller on the WayPixel costmap reaches SPL 63.63 vs 51.48 with object-level costmaps, and PixelReact reaches 81.77. Swapping LightGlue for MASt3R inside the object-level pipeline gives no gain, so the improvement comes from the representation, not the matcher. EMST sparse connectivity and 10x node subsampling cut edges from 4.6M to 24k with equal or better SPL (78.62 vs 74.78), and using all correspondences hurts.
method: MASt3R backbone (frozen): pairwise pixel correspondences plus per-pixel relative 3D point maps in the first image's frame

Pixel-based topological map: nodes are matched pixels; inter-frame edges have cost 0 (window of previous frames); intra-frame edges are weighted by 3D Euclidean distance; matched nodes can be merged to bound memory
Graph sparsification: random 10x subsampling of correspondences (node culling) and Euclidean MST (or Delaunay 3D) intra-frame connectivity instead of exhaustive edges

Localization and planning: match the query against a submap around the localization index (oracle retriever in simulation); precompute Dijkstra costs to the goal; find bridging map pixels; pick the reference image with minimum median cost; transfer costs to the matched query pixels
Dense WayPixel costmap: propagate costs to unmatched query pixels via min(3D distance + matched-pixel cost), then encode with sinusoidal embeddings
PixelReact controller: conv encoder plus MLP decoder (ObjectReact architecture) predicting 10 BEV waypoints, trained with L2 imitation loss on HM3Dv0.2 shortest-path trajectories

setting.backbone: frozen MASt3R + PixelReact (conv encoder + MLP, trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: Habitat HM3Dv0.2 shortest-path trajectories (same data as ObjectReact); MASt3R is pre-trained and frozen
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB (sensor height 0.4 m); map from a prior RGB image sequence
setting.action_space: predicted local BEV waypoints (10 future 2D waypoints with yaw)
setting.privileged: ground-truth localization (index of nearest map image, oracle retriever) and oracle stop in simulation

numbers.extra: submap radius 4, subsample 1; GT localization; oracle stop; 300 steps, 1m success radius

numbers_note: Only the HM3D-IIN val split (36 scenes, one episode each) is evaluated. Imitate results differ between Table 1 (81.77) and Table 2 (93.94) because the submap settings differ.
results: On HM3D-IIN, MASt3R-Nav averages SPL 52.79 / SSPL 60.24 over four tasks, against ObjectReact's 33.36 / 44.71. It roughly doubles the object-relative methods on Alt Goal and Shortcut but is weaker on Reverse (23.25 vs ObjectReact's 30.00), where MASt3R picks wrong reference images under low overlap. It also works on a real P3DX robot.
limitations: Poor Reverse performance: MASt3R gives similar inlier counts for true and false matches under low visual overlap, so it selects wrong reference images
Simulation uses GT localization/oracle retriever and an oracle stop; the real-world demo is qualitative only
Map construction is slower and heavier than ObjectReact (294 s vs 136 s on three floors), with thousands of pixel nodes
